where: ch28-demand-sizing 28.6, bullet 'Count two kinds of demand separately'
current: Delivered protein is what an ingredient maker sells; displaced meat protein is what the supply-security and welfare cases need. The first is about eight times the second on the benchmark path in 2035.
proposed: Count three things separately: protein delivered (what an ingredient maker sells), meat protein displaced (supply security) and animals spared and CO2e avoided (what welfare and climate funders count). Import substitution is 60% of delivered protein in 2035 but spares no animals and avoids about no CO2e. Nearly all animals spared are chickens and ducks; about half the CO2e comes from the 8.5% of meat that is beef and buffalo.

where: ch28-demand-sizing 28.6, 'For each reader', International organisations and funders
current: A funder whose goal is fewer animals raised should test the cheapest-looking route first: whether canteen chay days or promotion of chay practice add meat-free occasions without compensation.
proposed: Match the route to your unit and your rules. Welfare funders: canteens spare the most animals per tonne of protein (about 1,100 at the national dish mix, about 2,800 if chicken dishes are replaced, about 80 if pork dishes are); added chay days spare the most in total but are unmeasured. The funders we checked that pay for menu or chay-day work either do not cover Vietnam (ReRoot Asia, Lever, Sinergia, Good Food Fund) or exclude diet change (ACE Movement Grants from September 2026; Nova Vista); Humane World is the one implementer with Vietnam staff. Market-shaping funders: procurement of a canteen protein ingredient and naming and GMO rules, not chay days. Climate funders: totals are small (about 0.14 Mt CO2e a year by 2035). Development finance: import substitution for its import bill and industrial value, not for displacement.
